reason: Both answers cover the main moves: change the evaluation axis, reframe breadth as cost, pick a wedge, position as a complement, and qualify out bad-fit buyers. B adds things that would change what the asker does next. It says to get in before the RFP is written. It says the wedge must be a weakness the incumbent can't fix without hurting its core business. It suggests conceding openly, and it gives a diagnostic of reviewing the last 10 losses to tell a positioning problem from a table-stakes gap. A has a good point about the incumbent having written the RFP and a concrete walk-away rule. It also includes a shaky claim, that incumbents are customizable because they lack opinions. B is more complete on the key points and more actionable.
